subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - milestone follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-02-25T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - draft and next steps

Hi Sarah / Michael —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation on your use case and compliance constraints. Per our call, I’m sharing a brief Mutual Action Plan (attached) with the initial milestone we discussed focused on Data Handling & Compliance. This milestone is intended to get us to a procurement-ready posture for PHI/PII-sensitive workflows.

Short recap of the MAP milestone (Data handling & compliance):
- Objective: Define and validate retention, logging/audit requirements, and any PHI/PII constraints for the integration.
- Target completion: 2026-03-18 (engineering & compliance sign-off)
- Owner: Acme Health (compliance) + Redwood (security & implementation) — see responsibilities below.
- Dependencies: SOC 2 evidence review, network/VPC setup, and acceptance of data minimization approach.

Draft responsibilities (please confirm or update):
- Acme Health (Sarah / Michael): provide retention policy, list of data classes considered PHI/PII, and required audit-log retention windows.
- Redwood (Dev): provide data flow diagram, logging capabilities, and options for on-prem/private deployment if needed.
- Redwood (Marissa / Dylan): coordinate procurement and legal (SLA/terms) once compliance items are resolved.

Open items from today’s call:
1) Whether Acme will allow tokenized identifiers vs raw PHI in requests (impacting retention).
2) Desired retention window for logs/audit trails (30/90/365 days).
3) Any required redaction/transform rules pre-ingest.

Next steps:
- Sarah: share retention policy + compliance questionnaire answers by EOD Tue (2026-03-03).
- Dev: share data flow diagram and logging options by Wed (2026-03-04).
- Marissa/Dylan: update MAP and HubSpot deal once items arrive.

Attached: MAP-draft-v1.docx (map with milestone table), SOC2-report-2025.pdf (for initial review).

Thanks — I’ll check in on Thursday to sync progress.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - draft and next steps

Marissa / team —

Quick technical follow-up based on the call:
- We can support both tokenized identifiers and raw fields, but tokenization reduces retention surface and simplifies audit obligations.
- Logging: Redwood can emit request/response hashes plus metadata (request id, timestamp, model, route) and keep full payload logging only in private deployments. For hosted customers, we recommend 90-day logs by default; for PHI workloads we typically move to private deployment or a dedicated retention config.
- Audit trails: we provide immutable append-only logs with export via S3 and a queryable interface for up to 365 days for Dedicated/Private plans.

I’m attaching a quick data flow sketch (inline below) and can produce a formal diagram by EOD Wed. If Acme requires field-level redaction prior to hitting our runtime, we should confirm whether redaction will be performed client-side or as a preprocessor in your VPC.

Action items (technical):
- Dev: produce formal data flow diagram + logging config options (due 2026-03-04).
- Acme: confirm tokenization vs raw fields and desired retention window.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@acmehealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - draft and next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary. A couple of clarifications from Compliance: 

1) We cannot send raw PHI identifiers off our environment without a BAAs and encryption at rest + strict key management. Our preference is tokenization client-side.
2) Audit log retention requirement: 2 years for any access logs related to PHI. Is that feasible with Redwood’s export/query model?
3) We need a diagram showing where logs are stored and how they’re protected (encryption, KMS, role separation).

If tokenization adds too much latency, we may consider a private deployment (VPC) and a BAA. Can you confirm costs/lead time for a private deployment option?

Thanks — Sarah
Senior Compliance Manager | Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - milestone follow-up

Sarah — thanks for the clarity. Summary of updates and revised milestone responsibilities based on your inputs: 

Updated milestone: Data handling & compliance (v1.1)
- Target completion: 2026-03-18 (compliance sign-off) — unchanged, pending quick turnaround on items below.
- Acme Health (Sarah / Michael): confirm tokenization approach (client-side) or request Private deployment + BAA. Provide retention policy doc by 2026-03-06.
- Redwood (Dev): deliver formal data flow diagram + logging/export mechanics; include KMS/HSM details and encryption-at-rest/motion description. ETA: 2026-03-04.
- Redwood (Marissa/Dylan): produce cost/lead-time estimate for Private/VPC deployment and BAA process. ETA: 2026-03-06.

Dependencies and gating items:
- SOC2 evidence review (attached) — Redwood to provide any additional artifacts requested by Acme compliance.
- Legal: BAA negotiation timeline if Private deployment chosen.
- Network: VPC peering or customer-managed outbound allowlisting for hosted flows.

Next immediate steps (this week):
1) Dev to upload data flow diagram + logging option doc (by EOD today).
2) Marissa to add Private deployment cost/lead-time note and update MAP; share updated MAP + HubSpot note once complete (by Fri 2026-03-06).
3) Sarah to confirm retention window and tokenization decision (by 2026-03-06).

I’ll attach the updated MAP once I’ve incorporated Dev’s diagram and the Private deployment estimate. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute deep dive with our security engineer — open to times Thurs/Fri.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
